thread:
Tara M: FYI customer cust-2211 opened an urgent ticket — their service hit a wave of 429s around 11:45 UTC after a scheduled data replay. They attached a curl and a list of example request ids.

Samir B: drop the ids here and i'll grep the gateway. which endpoint + model?

Tara M: endpoint /v1/generate, app=personalization, model=encoder-pro-2.0, sample ids r-20260320-44a1, r-20260320-44a2. They said they fired ~12 parallel calls from one key during the replay.

MetricsBot: alert: throttle_rate > 1% for api_key=cust-2211 between 11:44-11:49 UTC.

Samir B: pulling token metrics now. seeing tokens_consumed spike: approx 210k tokens/min at 11:45. Their committed rate is 150k tokens/min with a 90s burst window to 300k. Token bucket dropped to zero -> gateway returned 429 (throttle_type=burst).

Kevin O (oncall): do our dashboards show attribution broken down by api_key + route + model? We need to produce a short customer report.

Emily P: yes, panels to check:
- Quota: tokens_by_key_route (PromQL: sum by(api_key,route,model)(increase(tokens_consumed_total[1m])))
- Throttles: throttle_by_key_route (PromQL: sum by(api_key,route)(increase(throttle_counter_total[5m])))
- Inflight: in_flight_by_key (PromQL: sum by(api_key)(in_flight_infers))

Tara M: customer insists they didn't exceed what their console showed. they replayed older requests and thought these shouldn't be billed.

Amber C (billing): replayed requests count as normal consumption unless tagged billing_exempt. Their account has no exemptions. Also check for client-side retries; retries can double-count quickly.

Samir B: logs for r-20260320-44a1:
```
[11:45:10.112] route=/v1/generate api_key=cust-2211 model=encoder-pro-2.0 tokens=9800 latency=1600ms throttle=1 reason=burst_exhausted
[11:45:11.478] route=/v1/generate api_key=cust-2211 model=encoder-pro-2.0 tokens=10240 latency=1710ms throttle=1 reason=burst_exhausted
```
Tara M: customer attached their curl repro:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer key-cust-2211" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{"model":"encoder-pro-2.0","prompt":"...","max_tokens":1500}'
```
Emily P: prefix cache hit was ~1% during the window so caching wasn't helping. Autoscaler didn't kick; utilization was high and no fallback policy was configured on their route.

Samir B: i'll run an export for 11:40-11:50 filtered by api_key cust-2211 with fields: request_id,timestamp,tokens_consumed,throttle_flag,throttle_reason,route,model,response_code. That should make attribution crystal clear.

OpsBot: export job queued (id export-9912). ETA around 90s.

Kevin O: can we also surface per-request token count panel in Console? support often needs that to justify throttles to customers.

Emily P: it's not exposed today; backend stores per-request tokens but Console aggregates it. product: prioritize a light-weight CSV export UI and a panel that shows top N requests by token usage for a given time window.

Amber C: for remediation we can temporarily raise their burst window +100k tokens for 45m (adj id: bill-temporary-2023). that buys breathing room while SEs implement client mitigations.

Tara M: please apply and i'll let the customer know. also they want guidance to avoid this: recommended per-key concurrency cap, backoff guidance, smaller max_tokens, or enable fallback to encoder-pro-small.

Samir B: remediation checklist i suggest:
1) apply temporary burst increase (Amber).
2) export logs and provide CSV (Samir).
3) recommend client changes (Tara): limit parallelism to <=4, add exponential backoff with jitter, reduce max_tokens or chunk requests.
4) opt-in to model fallback (product).

MetricsBot: export-9912 complete, file=export-9912.csv (attached).

Samir B: analysis of CSV: 82% of 429 responses during window map to api_key=cust-2211 on route /v1/generate model=encoder-pro-2.0. Peak single-request token consumption was ~11k tokens. If you run 12 of those concurrently you blow through the burst allowance quickly.

Tara M: i'll attach the CSV to the customer email and include repro steps and headers to check. Repro steps for SEs/client:
- run 6 parallel curl requests with max_tokens=1500; you'll see throttles after ~45-70s.
- check 429 response headers: X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, X-Throttle-Reason, X-RateLimit-Policy.

Kevin O: note for ops: add an alert runbook link to the throttle dashboard so oncall can quickly run this attribution flow.

Emily P: filing docs PR for a short FAQ: "Why did my replay cause 429s?" including token math example and recommended console views. I'll ping devex for visibility.

Amber C: burst bump applied (bill-temporary-2023). I'll add a note about operational credit if they escalate, but we don't auto-credit for temporary allowances.

Tara M: sending customer email with attached CSV and suggested mitigations. i'll offer a 1:1 walk-through if needed.

Samir B: follow-ups: add conservative per-route concurrency rule for this app (workaround) in routing rules: if api_key==cust-2211 and in_flight_by_key>4 -> return 429 with X-RateLimit-Policy=concurrency.

OpsBot: thread archived at 12:17 UTC.

Kevin O: postmortem note: consider adding a per-request tokens heatmap on Console and a short alert that triggers when single-request token > configurable threshold. good candidate for next sprint.

DocsBot: PR created for FAQ (pr/455).
